newsitem.title: USA: Nasdaq ignores IBM, powers to record close.
newsitem.headline: Nasdaq ignores IBM, powers to record close.

text.p: Nasdaq stocks charged to a record closing high on the back of rallying technology stocks, ignoring a sharp downturn in computer giant International Business Machines Corp.
The Nasdaq composite ended up about 11 points, or 0.8 percent, at 1388. It was the index's fourth consecutive record high close.

Nasdaq tech heavyweights Microsoft Corp, up 2-3/8 to 97-3/8, and Intel Corp, up 4-1/16 to 152-1/8, fueled the drive. Traders said the companies were still finding buyers following their strong earnings reports last week.
"Mostly there's continued strength in techland," said Arnie Owen, director of equities at Kaufman Brothers.
The day's action was an indication that Microsoft and Intel have challenged, if not overtaken, IBM as indicators of technology stock sentiment, traders said.
IBM ended off 10 at 158 after its fourth quarter earnings report disappointed investors.
Veritas Software rose 6-3/4 to 51 after signing a licensing pact with Sun Microsystems.
Steris Corp dropped 8-3/4 to 29-1/4 after warning its quarterly results would fall below Wall Street estimates.
